Witty editorial advertising still life, 9:16 vertical Story frame, Diwali evening. On a pale ivory lime-plaster floor, three small hand-thrown terracotta diyas, each about 7cm across, burn with small steady flames in a gentle arc at the upper right. The bracelet lies open in a soft curve around their front, and every pastel stone holds a tiny warm reflection of the flames. Preserve the bracelet from reference 1 exactly, with its stones built exactly as in reference 2: a continuous line of square cushion-cut stones about 5mm each in the repeating order aqua blue, soft pink, pale yellow, every stone framed by its own fine pave halo of tiny clear stones, linked in rhodium silver tone with a fold-over clasp. Do not redesign, restyle, resize or add anything; the stones must stay cushion-cut pastel stones in the repeating aqua, pink, yellow order, never all one colour, never round, never other colours, and no two neighbouring stones are ever the same colour; every stone keeps its halo of two rows of very fine pave, the halo about a third as wide as the centre stone on each side; each stone is held by four short round bead claws flush at its corners, never long prongs or spikes. Only the background, surface and lighting change. CRITICAL SCALE: each stone is about 5mm, the size of a peppercorn, and each stone in its halo is about 8mm square; the bracelet is about 18cm long and only about 8mm wide, a slim line. The diyas are about nine times the width of the bracelet's line. COPY SPACE: the upper left third is calm, softly glowing empty plaster for a headline. LIGHT: the warm diya flames as the key, a soft cool fill from the left so the aqua and pink keep their colour, one small hard kicker on the silver. ABSENCE LIST: No text, no letters, no logo, no watermark, no price tag anywhere in frame. No hands, no people. No second piece of jewellery. No border, no vignette: the photograph fills the frame edge to edge.

STORY FRAME: tall 9:16. The top quarter of the frame is calm, empty background for a headline and the bottom fifth is calm, empty surface for a price line; the jewellery sits in the middle band, at the same true small scale.

Witty editorial advertising still life, 9:16 vertical Story frame, for an Indian demi-fine jewellery brand. On a pale ivory lime-plaster surface, half a pomegranate lies cut face up at the upper right edge of the frame, its glistening deep-red arils packed in white pith; seven loose arils have rolled out across the plaster. ONE single ruby baguette tennis bracelet, CLOSED with its box clasp shut, lies as ONE continuous unbroken oval loop in the lower middle, the loose arils around it, its stones exactly the same deep red as the seeds.

THE PRODUCT: IMAGE 1 is our approved product photograph and the authority on this exact piece: its construction, size, metal colour and stone colour; ignore its plaster cube, background and light. IMAGE 2 is the supplier photograph of the same piece, for construction detail only; ignore everything else in it. Preserve the piece exactly: do not redesign, restyle, resize or add anything. CONSTRUCTION LOCK: A TENNIS BRACELET: ONE continuous line of deep RUBY-RED rectangular BAGUETTE stones set CROSSWISE, side by side like the rungs of a ladder, each stone held by gold claws at its four corners, edge to edge with no gaps, about 5mm wide; a gold box clasp with a fold-over safety tongue. Warm 18k gold tone. The stones stay rectangular baguettes set crosswise, never round, never set lengthways; all stones ruby red, never pink, never orange.

SCALE TEST: Each baguette is 5 by 2.5mm; each pomegranate aril is about 9mm, a little larger than one stone; the closed bracelet is a 5.5cm oval, 5mm wide. There is exactly ONE bracelet and ONE clasp; the loop is never broken into two pieces and never has loose ends. The jewellery keeps its true small size against the referent; it dominates by light and isolation, never by being enlarged.

COPY SPACE: The upper left third of the frame is calm, empty ivory plaster, softly lit, for a headline.

LIGHT: soft large window light from the upper left, one soft natural shadow, plus ONE small hard specular kicker from the right, so the metal shows a crisp bright edge and a dark rolled edge on every curve and every stone carries internal sparkle and one pure-white catchlight, never flat colour. Honest macro optics: the jewellery is needle-sharp and the scene falls softly out of focus behind it. Real texture everywhere: grain, fibre, dust, believable imperfection, nothing plastic. 

ABSENCE LIST: No text, no letters, no logo, no watermark, no price tag anywhere in frame. No hands, no people. No second piece of jewellery. No border, no vignette: the photograph fills the frame edge to edge.
